A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEGO/DetPool grasping study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison; relocated sections and renumbered tables can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation and physical-robot grasping results in Tables 1–3, alongside scaling studies and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds geometric-similarity analysis, robustness experiments, additional baselines, pushing results, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The MVP vision encoder, segmentation-based attention restriction, object-token pooling, transformer policy, L1 loss, and default absolute-joint control remain unchanged. New horizon and control-mode experiments are ablations; the pushing experiment does not document a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds push-to-target manipulation, requiring sustained contact rather than grasp-and-lift behavior, while retaining toy training and YCB evaluation. Appendix B also adds controlled evaluation scenarios involving reduced illumination, multiple clutter objects, random or lookalike distractors, and inaccurate segmentation inputs. The original robot embodiments and grasping object sets remain.

E2.justification: Appendix C.1 and Table 12 add GROOT (Zhu et al., 2023) and DexGraspVLA (Zhong et al., 2025) to the simulation comparisons at 250 and 2,500 demonstrations. These materially extend comparisons against other object-centric approaches. Existing VLA, pooling, and ShapeGrasp comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include Chamfer-distance grouping at the 33rd/66th percentiles, specified lighting reductions, 2–5 clutter objects, bounding-box IoU perturbations, and condition/prediction-length variations. The scaling study adds 5- and 15-toy subsets. OpenVLA-OFT documentation changes from batch size 2 to global batch size 16 across three setups; this is revised reporting, without establishing whether experiments were rerun or the earlier number was per-device.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of dependence on training-object geometry, lighting/clutter/distractor robustness, mask-error sensitivity, temporal conditioning and prediction horizons, and absolute versus delta control. Figure 4 further probes low-diversity training with 5 and 15 toys. The existing primitive, complexity, model-size, and color ablations remain; the color analysis moves from Appendix B to C.2.

E5.justification: New Table 6 reports success rates with 95% confidence intervals for geometric-similarity groups, whereas v1 reports point estimates. It also includes Chamfer-distance dispersion statistics. The confidence-interval calculation is not explained, and no increase in independent training runs or new seed protocol is documented.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–5 and the color-ablation values are retained, but substantial new results appear. At 2,500 demonstrations, v2 reports 67.21% success with clutter, 77.98% at 60% bounding-box IoU, and pushing success of 81.83% versus 75.77% for OpenVLA-OFT (Tables 9, 11, 14). Table 16 adds 37.02% for delta control versus 80.00% for absolute control. Figure 4 changes the stated sufficient toy count from 25 to 15. These are added findings, not improved scores on the retained evaluations.

T1.justification: The observation/action definitions, policy mapping, and training-loss mathematics are retained. Neither version presents a theorem or proof contribution. The new Chamfer-distance stratification is an empirical analysis, without a new mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: generalizable grasping from four primitive shapes, DetPool as the key representation mechanism, data-efficient scaling, and approximately 67% real-world YCB success. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 newly interprets performance as weakly dependent on geometric similarity, attributes mask-error tolerance to patch-level pooling, and argues that longer conditioning and absolute control provide more stable prediction. It also extends the applicability discussion to contact-rich pushing and interprets the new baseline and robustness results. The existing limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 revises OpenVLA-OFT batch-size documentation and specifies ground-truth simulator depth for GROOT and bounding-box perturbations supplied to SAM in the new robustness test. Existing LEGO hyperparameters, hardware, teleoperation procedures, printing instructions, and project-access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Emukpere et al.'s object-centric representation work, GROOT, and DexGraspVLA, and expands its contrast with large pretrained object-centric VLAs. Most research positioning is retained, including the comparison with OTTER. Moving Related Work from Section 2 to Section 5 is structural rather than a positioning change.

P1.justification: Related Work moves after Experiments, and the expanded appendices receive new subdivisions. V2 also edits the humanoid π0-FAST implementation prose and updates authorship, affiliations, and conference headers. Most existing prose, including the abstract, method, conclusion, and limitations, remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds nine result tables covering geometry, robustness, baselines, pushing, horizons, and control modes. Figure 4 is redrawn with additional curves and legend entries and without its former zoomed inset. Table 2 reorders and groups rows, and figures and tables are redistributed through the document. Existing overview and hardware illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central generalization argument: geometric-similarity analysis and mask/scene perturbations address important untested explanations and sensitivities in v1, while direct object-centric comparisons and pushing evaluation broaden the evidence. Some new interpretations overstate their tables—for example, DexGraspVLA does not outperform OpenVLA-OFT at 250 demonstrations in Table 12—and uncertainty reporting remains limited. These shortcomings qualify the conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical scrutiny.
